reviewMethod: Complete line-by-line semantic review of the deterministic repository-audit authority, including Git-object data flow, exact-head binding, fail-closed behavior, workflow permissions, action pinning, negative-test adequacy and completion-claim boundaries.

residualRisks.statement: This bounded slice reviews nine Batch 1 audit-authority files only; test authorities remain assigned to Batch 12 and all other repository paths retain their pending status.

The workflow guard intentionally implements only the governed repository-audit YAML shape rather than the complete YAML specification; any future workflow restructuring requires policy and negative-fixture updates.

reviewNotes: Triggers, read-only permissions, exact PR-head checkout, non-persistent credentials, expected-SHA propagation, authority verification, manifest regeneration, tests and immutable artifact upload were reviewed as one fail-closed sequence.
All third-party actions are pinned to full commit SHAs and the artifact name is bound to the exact reviewed head.
All scripts, dependency pins, engine constraints and override declarations were reviewed; the audit commands remain exact and separated between generation, authority checking, verification and tests.

The added ESLint, secret-scanning, operational-recovery and production supply-chain commands bind their permanent guards to focused tests; supply-chain:check now executes both its source authority and 44 host-policy tests, while env:check composes the existing environment validator with the production CSP connection validator.
The release path uses npm ci and governed checks; mutable developer convenience commands remain outside release authority.

reviewNotes: Filesystem scope, ignored runtime outputs, import extraction, local resolution, entrypoint reachability, artifact heuristics, dependency ownership, bounded reporting and non-deletion warning were reviewed line by line.

findings.attackPath: A package binary referenced after whitespace in package scripts was not recognized because the template literal consumed the regex backslash, producing a false unreferenced-dependency lead.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository hygiene evidence must not classify an owned dependency as unreferenced because of a malformed scanner boundary.
findings.evidence: The former template literal used [\s;&|] in source semantics that evaluated as [s;&|]; the final source escapes the backslash and the authority guard preserves that contract.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent authority check must reject removal of the escaped whitespace boundary and the hygiene report must continue to execute successfully.

reviewNotes: The guard verifies workflow authority, committed evidence schema/batch identity, runtime-artifact hygiene exclusion, both package-binary whitespace boundaries and exact package command ownership before manifest generation.

findings.attackPath: A later scanner edit could regress only the leading package-binary whitespace class while leaving the trailing class intact, allowing the former single-substring guard to pass and miss package binaries after shell separators.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository hygiene evidence must preserve both package-binary boundary classes so dependency ownership is not undercounted.
findings.evidence: The former authority check required only one escaped boundary occurrence; the remediated guard counts the source occurrences and requires at least two.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent authority check must fail if either escaped package-binary whitespace boundary is removed.

findings.attackPath: A required checkout, verification or artifact contract could be removed from executable YAML and preserved only as a comment while the former substring guard still returned success.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository audit evidence must fail closed when an exact-head workflow control is not executable.
findings.evidence: The previous guard used unrestricted includes() checks; the final implementation parses the governed YAML structure and validates exact effective step nodes, keys, values and sequence.
findings.verificationRequirement: Negative fixtures must move each governed contract into a comment and observe a policy failure; the unchanged real workflow must pass.

findings.attackPath: A second workflow job could declare permissions: write-all and execute an unpinned action while the previous parser inspected only the governed manifest job and top-level mapping.
findings.affectedInvariant: Every job in the repository-audit workflow must remain inside the exact read-only and action-pinned authority.
findings.evidence: The parser now rejects every permissions node except the single top-level mapping and requires jobs to contain exactly the governed manifest job.
findings.verificationRequirement: A negative fixture must append a second job with scalar write-all permissions and an unpinned action, then observe a structural policy failure.

findings.attackPath: An if: false condition on manifest generation, verification or upload could skip required evidence while the previous parser ignored arbitrary scalar step properties.
findings.affectedInvariant: Every governed audit step must execute unconditionally whenever the workflow job runs.
findings.evidence: The parser now accepts only env, run, uses and with on governed steps, so if and other skip-capable properties fail structural validation.
findings.verificationRequirement: Negative fixtures must add if: false independently to generation, verification and upload and observe policy failure for each mutation.
